title: Measure the zodiac figure rings before accepting geometric label rotations
statement: Two blind torso-center readings cover six Yale wheels and 153 figures in eleven fully counted rings. All eleven have one clockwise rotation within the main measurement envelope and their upper mean discrepancy is below the 6/n-hour screen. In the formerly failing f72v1 outer ring, measured mean discrepancy is 0.1825 h (envelope 0.1259–0.2621 h), versus nominal 0.3225 h and cutoff 0.3000 h. Moving the estimated centers on a 49-point grid within 20 crop pixels preserves all eleven best rotations. The expanded upper discrepancy crosses the screen in the inner rings of f73r and f73v; f72v1 outer remains below (upper 0.2815 h). A doubtful fold figure leaves f72v3 outer at 17/18 or 18/18 between readers. Including the candidate provisionally gives 0.1397 h at cutoff 0.3333 h. The native crop still leaves limb and torso joins unresolved. The f72v1 outer rotation pairs the crowned torso at 0.4146 h with locus f72v1.8, whose ZL clock is 01:45, a 1.3354 h residual. Two local visual reviews prefer different physical word groups and see no definitive word-to-star connector. The annotation records and their agreement scores are retained as published.
check: Recompute the twelve ring comparisons from the stored reader coordinates and the first pinned ZL clock marker of each fleet-fable locus. Resolve the obscured f72v3 torso from an independent view of the fold and cross-check f72v1.8 against the native scan and first-glyph coordinates. For each visually established label attachment, save a separate updated record with the old locus and a crop showing the visual cue. Compare the agreed attachments between seats before using any of these annotations in a picture-text test.
protocol:
# Blind torso-center measurements of six zodiac wheels

Each independent reader sees only named scan crops with a coordinate grid.
Readers mark the inner medallion boundary extrema and the torso centers of
every ring figure visible, without labels, clocks, expected counts or other
readings. Written words and stars are ignored during this pass. Record any
ambiguous figures or arcs. Points are measured to the nearest 5 crop pixels.

The medallion center is the midpoint of the two x extrema and the two y
extrema. Use clockwise bearing from image north and convert to 12 hours.
Only compare a full ring whose two counts match the number of submitted
fleet-fable objects. Sort each reading clockwise and align the two readings
by the cyclic shift minimizing total squared point separation, before any
label overlay. No reversal for reader pairing. Coordinates with a reader
separation larger than 0.22 times the median figure radius raise a visual
adjudication flag. Treat partial readings and uncertainty explicitly.

Use the median point and center of the two readers (their midpoint), and
start figure index zero at the torso nearest the meridian facing image north.
Compare all clockwise offsets to the initial ZL clock markers on the original
fleet-fable label loci. Retain the same 6/n-hour discrepancy threshold as
P-L4-060. Report full enumerations, literal figure-index label mappings, and
the best reverse-order offset as a control. Report offsets relative to the
chosen geometric index zero, which can differ from hand-keyed index zero.

To estimate sensitivity under reader disagreement and rounding, add half
the reader-to-reader Euclidean separation to a conservative 5*sqrt(2) pixels
for each paired point and center. Divide their sum by the radius and take
arcsin to bound each angular perturbation, capping at half a turn for a
degenerate radius. Apply these bounds separately to the shortest distance
for each figure in every shift and average. Any candidate lower bound at
or below the smallest upper bound stays ambiguous. This is a declared
sensitivity envelope, without a coverage probability.

Clock positions act as rough geometric metadata. Inspect a label attachment
separately on the visible scans before re-keying annotations. Keep original
records. An agreement increase by itself gives no attachment evidence.
center_sensitivity_protocol: Around the midpoint estimate, apply every common center displacement (dx,dy) on a five-pixel grid inside radius 20 crop pixels. Hold the geometrically keyed index zero fixed. Recompute angular point estimates at each center, adding the primary point-wise envelope to check the discrepancy screen under this stress test.

notes: Primary boundary follows the faint circular ink rule immediately around the central artwork, on the artwork-facing side of the surrounding band. The alternative follows the artwork-facing edge of the hatched border on the farther side of that band.
The primary rule is especially faint at top and right, and the fold affects the left part of the alternative edge. Boundary extrema are visual estimates with about 10–20 crop pixels of uncertainty.

The crease partly covers inner figures around one and seven o’clock. Included because each surviving outline establishes a separate figure, with torso uncertainty near 15–25 crop pixels. No additional distinct figures are inferred in the wider outer gap at the bottom.
Boundary points follow the outside edge of the hatched rim facing the inner figured ring. The medallion also has a faint inner circular trace.
The page fold and nearby basket contours obscure the western rim. The southwestern inner torso at [480, 1035] overlaps the fold, so its center is especially approximate.
Nineteen outer torsos are visually distinct. The southern gap between [930, 1380] and [660, 1380] is wider than the adjacent gaps.
Primary boundary follows the faint circular ink rule immediately around the central artwork. The alternative follows the facing rule on the farther side of the narrow band surrounding it.
Part of the primary right and lower arc is hard to follow where ink overlaps. The lower outline and the alternative left extremum have approximately 10–20 crop pixels of uncertainty.

The hole at roughly three o’clock obscures part of the inner annulus. The partly affected figure below it has a recoverable torso and is included. I could not distinguish another torso in the damaged area.
Boundary points follow the thin exterior medallion rim facing the inner figured ring. A fainter inner circular trace is also visible.
An oval opening near [1045, 740] interrupts the eastern inner sector. The distinct torso immediately below it, [960, 800], remains visible. The material within the opening is ambiguous.
The left side of the outer ring has lower contrast, especially around [205, 840] and [210, 630]. The northern torso at [695, 275] falls just west of the north axis.

Extrema are on the outer circular medallion stroke adjacent to the feet of the inner figures. The smaller stroke closer to the central image is also visible; the outer medallion stroke is clearer to trace. The lowest portion is faint.

Torso centers on the east of the outer ring around (1050,600) and (1080,765), and southwest around (175,910), are distinct but their ink outlines are weak; local uncertainty is approximately 10–20 px.
Extrema follow the continuous outer perimeter of the central medallion adjacent to the inner figures’ feet. Its lower arc is particularly faint.
A smaller visible contour immediately around the central illustration has approximate extrema left [465,725], top [600,585], right [745,725], bottom [605,865].

Outer centers [1055,590] and [1055,755] are faint by the right fold, but the torsos are distinguishable. Estimated torso position uncertainty is roughly 10 to 15 pixels there and about 5 to 10 pixels for most other figures.

Extrema are on the outer circular medallion stroke adjacent to the feet of the inner figures. The west arc is difficult to follow through the paper distortion; extrema uncertainty is approximately 10–20 px.

The inner figures at about (365,665), (375,805), and (415,945) are partly faded or distorted toward the western fold, but distinct body or limb outlines support their inclusion. Their torso points are approximate to 15–25 px.

An outline near (280,380) in the outer northwest ring may be a folded-over figure. It straddles the dark vertical fold, so I omitted it because its separate torso is not secure. The outer east figure centered around (1205,690) is recoverable from the torso and legs, with its head toward the edge. The ink near (1220,960) is also weak and partly in the right-hand margin, and I could not establish a separate figure there.
Extrema follow the continuous outer perimeter of the central medallion adjacent to the inner figures’ feet. The lower arc and the leftmost stretch are light.
Outer [285,350] is probable from the trunk and lower outlines crossing the deep left fold, with a poorly resolved head. Its center is uncertain by roughly 15 to 25 pixels.

Outer [1205,680] and [1195,835] have visible trunks but low-contrast heads affected by the right fold. Inner [380,655] and [375,810] cross a shadowed area. Centers in these regions are uncertain by roughly 10 to 20 pixels. Other centers are approximate to about 5 to 10 pixels.
The outer figure [690,200] straddles the north ray within the center uncertainty. It is listed first by the measured torso midpoint.

The narrow central perimeter is faint and discontinuous. The eastern extreme follows the most distinct trace. The other extrema, especially north and south, were inferred from the adjacent arc and may vary by about 15 to 25 pixels.
The west and southwest inner torsos around [440,825], [455,910] and [510,1040] have faint or overlapping outlines. They are distinct figures, with centers uncertain by about 15 pixels.
Four separate figures above the outer circular track were excluded.

The central picture field is visible but none of the four individual extrema of a continuous central circle is securely traceable. The reported central boundary points estimate the envelope of the field, with approximately 15–25 pixels of uncertainty in each radial position.
The alternative is the outer edge of the inscription band between the two figure rings. The upper arc has a small break near its apex, and the point given is adjacent to that break.

The southwest inner outlines at [540,1025] and lower outer outlines at [600,1280] are faint. Their torso centers are approximate to about 15–25 pixels. The ring membership of the reported figures is distinguishable.
Four complete or partly faded figures above the wheel are excluded. The closest outer torso to due north is just west of the north ray and appears last in clockwise order.

The western central arc is visible. The other extrema use partly interrupted traces, with uncertainty of about 15 to 25 pixels. A shorter inner arc is locally visible near the top, about 20 pixels below the recorded northern perimeter.

The inner figure around [590,980] is partly obscured by a dark blotch and the one around [725,985] has faint outlines. The outer figures near [950,1145] and [755,1220] are also faint. Their centers may vary by about 15 to 25 pixels.
Four separate figures above the outer circular track were excluded, including pale ones.

A faint arc is discernible along the upper-left central boundary. The reported left and top points are approximate, and the right and bottom points are extrapolated across indistinct ink with roughly 15–25 pixels of uncertainty.
The alternative is the inner edge of the inscription band between the two figure rings. It is easier to trace than the central boundary, although parts of the right and lower arcs are faded.

The inner southwest figure at [610,985] has a stained head area but a discernible torso outline. The outer lower-right figures near [1090,990] and [945,1140] are faded. Torso centers there are approximate to about 15–25 pixels.
Four figures above the ring, including the faint upper-left one, are excluded.

f72v3_fold_candidate_only.reread: A rounded contour and two descending strokes meet the fold. The native scan did not resolve a separate torso or continuous limb connection for reader A.

reader_a.description: Dense outer arc ink above the star, possible final y-shaped glyph, obscured remaining strokes. Ray approaches a rim line.

reader_b.description: Inner interfigure group behind the crowned torso, initial o-like loop then a gallows. Nearby figures have similarly placed groups.

f72v1_crown_visual_check.decisions: No physical attachment was visually established. Earlier labels and picture agreements are preserved, with the ZL clock residual disclosed.
